replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed threats against this design:

1. Automated abuse of a reachable entry point — design has "Partners upload CSV files of orders to our SFTP server"; brute force / credential abuse of that drop is already covered by listed threat 4 (and flooding/volume abuse by listed threat 1). Covered.
2. Staff/admin/moderator screens showing partner-supplied content — the design names no internal console, review queue or admin view ("A parser job imports each file into the orders database" only). Thing not present; nothing to report.
3. Privileged actions with no record of who did it — present as bulk order creation; already covered by listed threat 7 ("No link between an imported order and the partner upload it came from").
4. Personal/financial pages a browser, proxy or CDN could cache — design describes no web page, download endpoint or HTTP response at all. Thing not present.
5. Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV/spreadsheet exports, emails, headers or another interpreter — present, and already covered by listed threat 3 (SQL concatenation plus "fields beginning with = or + are executed as formulas when the orders are later exported to a spreadsheet").
6. Single-reviewer items: #1 duplicates listed threat 2; #2 duplicates listed threat 4; #3 (re-dropped/renamed duplicates) is the same harm as listed threat 5's "import the same file twice"; #4 (hostile filenames / traversal) depends on move/archive/shell behaviour the design never states — only "A parser job imports each file" — so it is build-dependent and not reportable.

No uncovered threat that the design text itself supports.
